audit.why: Emerald+ headline 52.85% over 1754 games matches MC_WR_TABLES.tahmkench.darius. No change.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 3 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo. It also tells the player to "lock Darius in place and Devour him", which is the impossible ordering.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] says full-tank Tahm "absorbs Noxian Guillotine's true damage" by having "enough HP and resistances that the true damage execute threshold is never reached".
audit.why: Guillotine is flagged trueDamage in the kit — resistances do nothing against it, so naming resistances as the answer is actively wrong. Only raw max health raises what he needs to finish you. (Darius's R is also not flagged execute in the kit; the kit reserves that flag for threshold executes such as Garen's Demacian Justice.)
audit.corrected: Re-anchored on max HP and stated plainly that its true damage ignores armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is named as the matchup-defining cooldown everywhere but never given a number, so "engage when it is down" has no length attached.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s. A 26-second rank-1 window is enormous relative to Tongue Lash at 7s — that ratio is the whole reason the bait-the-pull plan works, and the player cannot judge it without the figure.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees with itself: the content layer (and the packet levelChart) call Level 2 and Level 6 for Tahm Kench, while full.phases[1].side says "Skill" and full.phases[4].side says "Darius".
audit.why: Two views of the same chart render different owners for the same stage. Flagged rather than edited — I cannot establish from the kits which side is the intended one, and inventing a power shift at 6 would be worse than the inconsistency.
audit.corrected: Not edited. Reported for the user to reconcile.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online reliably — Tongue Lash slow into stun lets you lock Darius in place and Devour him before Hemorrhage can fully stack.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks come online reliably — let Tongue Lash land the third stack and Devour straight away — a Q at 3 stuns but eats the stacks Devour needs.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where you have to be honest — Darius gets his E cooldown back faster and you have no ultimate escape if he baits you into a full Hemorrhage stack without your stun ready. Respect the short-trade pattern: throw Tongue Lash, let Thick Skin eat the bleed, and only all-in when you already have stacks built. Never engage with zero stacks and cooldowns up; he will Apprehend, stack five bleeds, and Guillotine before your E shield saves you. At 6 your Abyssal Voyage adds global threat, but more importantly the threat of your gank assist makes Darius play more cautiously — use the breathing room to force another 3-stack combo and extend your lead.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where you have to be honest — Darius gets his E cooldown back faster and you have no ultimate escape if he baits you into a full Hemorrhage stack without your stun ready. Respect the short-trade pattern: throw Tongue Lash, let Thick Skin eat the bleed, and only all-in when you already have stacks built. Never engage with zero stacks and cooldowns up; he will Apprehend, stack five bleeds, and Guillotine before your E shield saves you. At 6 Devour arrives, but it wants its own three stacks, and a Q thrown at 3 stuns and burns them; the threat alone makes Darius cautious — use the breathing room to force another 3-stack combo and extend your lead.

edits.before: Two items in, Tahm Kench is essentially immune to the Darius kill pattern — your grey health absorbs the Hemorrhage bleed ticks faster than he can restack them, and a full Devour hold on a 6-item Darius still removes him from a teamfight for two seconds while your team collapses. His Noxian Guillotine loses its lethality when you have enough HP and resistances that the true damage execute threshold is never reached cleanly. Keep fishing 3-stack windows, peel your carries with Devour in teamfights, and use Abyssal Voyage to be wherever the next fight breaks out — Darius cannot follow globally and you outscale him in every meaningful late-game metric.
edits.after: Two items in, Tahm Kench is essentially immune to the Darius kill pattern — your grey health absorbs the Hemorrhage bleed ticks faster than he can restack them, and a full Devour hold on a 6-item Darius still removes him from a teamfight for two seconds while your team collapses. His Noxian Guillotine loses its lethality when you have enough HP and resistances that the true damage execute threshold is never reached cleanly. Keep fishing 3-stack windows, peel your carries with Devour in teamfights, and save Devour for whoever he ults — the ally shield lands before Guillotine does, and you outscale him in every meaningful late-game metric.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage adds global threat and makes Darius play scared near walls; your 3-stack combo still punishes any overextension and your E shield blocks his trading pattern.
edits.after: Devour arrives at 6 and wants three stacks of its own — a Q at 3 burns them; your 3-stack combo still punishes any overextension and your E shield blocks his trading pattern.

edits.before: Full tank Tahm Kench absorbs Noxian Guillotine's true damage without reaching the execute threshold, and a teamfight Devour on Darius wastes his R window entirely while your team punishes.
edits.after: Full tank Tahm Kench survives Noxian Guillotine on raw max HP — its true damage ignores your armour, and a teamfight Devour on Darius wastes his R window entirely while your team punishes.

edits.after: - Darius Apprehend: matchup-defining — His all-in start, down 26s at rank 1. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Systemic, beyond this matchup: "Abyssal Voyage" appears 182 times across champ-data/content/tahmkench.js. It is a removed ability — the live kit is W Abyssal Dive / R Devour. Every one of those lines is telling Tahm Kench players to use a global they do not have. Worth a dedicated pass over the whole file. Also: full.phases[1].side and full.phases[4].side disagree with the content-layer win[] chart for this matchup (see audit point 3).
